name: Brandy
description: Spirit distilled from wine or other fermented fruit and usually aged in oak. Rich and rounded, it is the base of the Sidecar, the Brandy Alexander and many classic punches.

name: Cognac
description: Grape brandy from the Cognac region of western France, double distilled in copper pot stills and aged in French oak. Graded VS, VSOP and XO by age.

name: Armagnac
description: Grape brandy from Gascony in south-west France, usually distilled once in a small column still and aged in local oak. Fuller and more rustic than cognac, with prune and spice notes.

name: Apple Brandy
description: Brandy distilled from fermented apple juice or cider, made in France, the USA, England and elsewhere. Fresh and fruity when young, richer and oakier with age.

name: Calvados
description: Apple brandy from Normandy, France, distilled from cider (sometimes with perry pears) and aged in oak. Tastes of baked apple, vanilla and spice.

name: Applejack
description: American apple brandy with roots in colonial New Jersey. Blended applejack mixes apple brandy with neutral spirit, while straight versions are all apple. The base of the Jack Rose.

name: Pisco
description: Unaged grape brandy from Peru and Chile. Peruvian pisco is distilled to proof from grapes such as Quebranta and Italia, giving a floral, grapey spirit for Pisco Sours and Pisco Punch.

name: Singani
description: Bolivian spirit distilled from Muscat of Alexandria grapes grown at high altitude. Clear, floral and aromatic, it is used much like pisco in sours and highballs.

name: Grappa
description: Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace, the skins and seeds left after winemaking. Usually clear and unaged with a grapey, earthy bite, though barrel-aged riserva styles exist.

name: Spanish Brandy
description: Grape brandy from Spain, mostly aged by the solera system in used sherry casks in Jerez or in oak in Catalonia. Tends to be soft and sweet-edged, with raisin, nut and caramel notes.

name: Brandy de Jerez
description: Spanish brandy aged in the sherry triangle of Andalusia using the solera system, in casks that previously held sherry. Dark, nutty and raisined.

name: Greek Brandy
description: Greek grape spirit in the Metaxa style, where aged wine distillates are blended with Muscat wine and botanicals. Smooth and slightly sweet, with floral and dried fruit notes.

name: Italian Brandy
description: Grape brandy from Italy, commonly distilled from Trebbiano wine and aged in oak. Generally soft and mellow, with vanilla and dried fruit notes.

name: Plum Brandy
description: Spirit distilled from fermented plums, known as slivovitz across Central and Eastern Europe. Usually clear and dry, with a strong stone fruit and almond aroma.

name: Eau-de-vie
description: Clear, unaged fruit brandy distilled from fermented fruit such as pear, cherry, raspberry or plum. Dry and intensely aromatic, and used in small measures to lift a drink.
photo_query: eau de vie fruit brandy bottles

name: Kirsch
description: Clear cherry eau-de-vie, also called kirschwasser, distilled from fermented whole cherries in Germany, Switzerland and Alsace. Dry, with cherry and a faint almond note from the stones.

name: Poire Williams
description: Clear eau-de-vie distilled from Williams (Bartlett) pears, made in France, Switzerland, Germany, Austria and the USA. Dry and strongly scented of ripe pear.
photo_query: Poire Williams eau de vie bottle

name: Framboise Eau-de-Vie
description: Clear, dry raspberry spirit made by macerating or fermenting raspberries and distilling them. Intensely perfumed and unsweetened, so not the same thing as raspberry liqueur.

name: Apricot Eau-de-Vie
description: Clear, dry spirit distilled from fermented apricots, known as barack in Hungary and Marillenbrand in Austria. Unsweetened, unlike apricot liqueur or apricot brandy liqueur.

name: Hennessy VS Cognac
description: The entry cognac from Hennessy, the largest cognac house, and a standard bar pour worldwide. Bold and oaky, with toasted almond, vanilla and grape notes.

name: Hennessy VSOP Cognac
description: Hennessy's VSOP, first made in 1817 and sold as Privilège. Rounder and softer than the VS, with vanilla, clove, cinnamon and candied fruit.

name: Hennessy XO Cognac
description: Hennessy's XO, created in 1870 and a familiar sight on back bars. A rich, powerful blend of older eaux-de-vie with dried fruit, cocoa, pepper and oak.

name: Rémy Martin VSOP Cognac
description: Fine Champagne cognac blended only from Grande and Petite Champagne grapes. Smooth and fruity, with vanilla, ripe apricot and baked apple. A common call for Sidecars.

name: Rémy Martin 1738 Accord Royal Cognac
description: Fine Champagne cognac that sits between Rémy Martin's VSOP and XO, aged in toasted oak. Round and rich, with plum, fig, toffee and baking spice.
image_query: Remy Martin 1738 Accord Royal Cognac bottle

name: Martell VS Cognac
description: Entry cognac from Martell, founded in 1715, bottled as VS Single Distillery. Light and fruity, with plum, apricot and candied lemon, and mixes easily.
image_query: Martell VS Single Distillery Cognac bottle

name: Martell VSOP Cognac
description: Martell's VSOP, aged in red oak barrels that previously held cognac. Soft and mellow, with ripe yellow fruit, quince, raisin and gentle wood spice.

name: Courvoisier VS Cognac
description: Entry cognac from Courvoisier of Jarnac, one of the four big cognac houses. Fresh and lively, with spring blossom, ripe pear and a light oak finish.

name: Pierre Ferrand 1840 Original Formula Cognac
description: Grande Champagne cognac bottled at 45 percent and modelled on a 19th century three star cognac, built for mixing. Grapey and bright, with honey, spice and enough strength for cocktails.
image_query: Pierre Ferrand 1840 Original Formula Cognac bottle

name: Pierre Ferrand Ambre Cognac
description: Grande Champagne cognac from Maison Ferrand, aged longer than a typical VSOP. Floral and fruity, with apricot, vanilla and rose, suited to sipping or stirred drinks.

name: H by Hine VSOP Cognac
description: Fine Champagne VSOP from Hine of Jarnac, blended with bartenders in mind. Light and floral, with apricot, jasmine and white pepper, and priced for mixing.
image_query: H by Hine VSOP Cognac bottle

name: Merlet Brothers Blend Cognac
description: Cognac blended by brothers Pierre and Luc Merlet at the family distillery in Saint-Sauvant. Fruity and supple, with peach, vanilla and light oak, made with cocktails in mind.

name: Frapin 1270 Cognac
description: Single estate Grande Champagne cognac from the Frapin family, who have grown grapes in the region since 1270. Fresh and floral, with vine flower, vanilla and light oak.

name: D'Ussé VSOP Cognac
description: VSOP cognac made at the Château de Cognac and a big seller in the USA. Bold and woody, with cinnamon, dried fruit and honey.

name: Méry Melrose VSOP Cognac
description: Certified organic, single estate cognac from the Grande Champagne cru. Elegant and floral, with dried apricot, vanilla and soft oak.
image_query: Mery Melrose Organic VSOP Cognac bottle

name: Seven Tails XO Brandy
description: French brandy blended from cognac, armagnac and other French grape brandies, then finished in port casks. Rich and fruity, with toasted vanilla, fig and blackberry.

name: St-Rémy VSOP Brandy
description: Widely sold French grape brandy, made since 1886 and aged in small oak barrels. Soft and approachable, with vanilla, ripe fruit and light oak. Common for cooking and mixing.

name: Three Barrels VSOP Brandy
description: French grape brandy and one of the biggest selling brandies in the UK. Smooth and rounded, with almond, walnut, candied fruit and ginger.
image_query: Three Barrels Rare Old French Brandy VSOP bottle

name: Tariquet VS Classique Bas-Armagnac
description: Young Bas-Armagnac from Domaine Tariquet, the Grassa family estate in Gascony. Lively and fruity, with prune, toasted bread and light oak, and priced for mixing.

name: Janneau VSOP Armagnac
description: VSOP from Janneau, an armagnac house founded in 1851 in Condom. Blends single and double distilled spirits for a smooth style with prune, vanilla and toasted oak.

name: Marie Duffau Napoléon Bas-Armagnac
description: Bas-Armagnac made by the Delord family and popular with American bartenders for its value. Warm and rounded, with prune, orange peel, caramel and spice.

name: Dartigalongue Un-Oaked Armagnac
description: Clear blanche armagnac from Dartigalongue in Nogaro, rested without any oak contact. Fresh and floral, with white fruit and pepper, and made for cocktails.

name: Christian Drouin Sélection Calvados
description: Young calvados from the Drouin family, distilled from cider with a share of perry pears. Fresh and fruity, with crisp apple and pear, and a common bar pour for mixing.

name: Christian Drouin Blanche de Normandie
match: Christian Drouin La Blanche Eau De Cidre
description: Unaged apple eau-de-vie distilled from cider by Christian Drouin. Clear and crisp, with fresh apple and a clean finish, used like a white spirit in cocktails.
image_query: Christian Drouin Blanche de Normandie bottle

name: Père Magloire VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge
description: Double distilled Pays d'Auge calvados from one of the best known calvados brands. Round and mellow, with baked apple, dried fruit and vanilla.
image_query: Pere Magloire VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge bottle

name: Boulard VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge
description: Pays d'Auge calvados from the Boulard family, double distilled in pot stills and aged in oak. Balanced, with ripe apple, vanilla and light wood spice.
image_query: Boulard VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge bottle

name: Dupont VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge
description: Estate calvados from Domaine Dupont, double distilled and aged around five years in oak. Bottled at 42 percent, with toasted oak, liquorice, vanilla and fresh apple.
image_query: Domaine Dupont VSOP Calvados Pays d'Auge bottle

name: Avallen Calvados
description: Young calvados from a brand built around sustainability, distilled at Domaine du Coquerel and aged two years in French oak. Fresh and apple forward, with vanilla and blossom.

name: Lemorton Réserve Calvados Domfrontais
description: Calvados from the Lemorton family in the Domfrontais, where a high share of perry pears goes into the cider. Column distilled, with bright pear, apple skin and light oak.

name: 30&40 Eau de Vie de Cidre
description: Apple spirit from 30&40, an independent bottler of Normandy brandies, bottled at 45 percent. Bright, crisp apple with herbal and spice notes, used like a young calvados in drinks.
image_query: 30&40 Eau de Vie de Cidre de Normandie bottle

name: Laird's Applejack
description: Blended applejack from Laird & Company, America's oldest licensed distillery. A mix of apple brandy and neutral grain spirit, light and mellow, with baked apple and caramel.

name: Laird's Straight Applejack 86
description: Straight apple brandy from Laird's, made entirely from apples and bottled at 86 proof. Fuller than the blended applejack, with fresh apple, vanilla and oak.

name: Laird's Bottled in Bond Straight Apple Brandy
description: All apple brandy from Laird's, aged at least four years and bottled at 100 proof. Robust, with baked apple, cinnamon and oak. The usual bartender choice for a Jack Rose.
image_query: Laird's Bottled in Bond Straight Apple Brandy 100 proof bottle

name: St. George California Reserve Apple Brandy
description: Apple brandy from St. George Spirits, pot distilled from California apples and aged in French and American oak. Bright apple, honey and baking spice.
image_query: St. George California Reserve Apple Brandy bottle

name: Somerset Cider Brandy 5 Year Old
description: English apple brandy distilled from cider at Burrow Hill in Somerset and aged five years in oak. Dry and appley, with toffee, spice and a warming finish.
image_query: Somerset Cider Brandy 5 Year Old bottle

name: BarSol Primero Quebranta Pisco
description: Peruvian pisco distilled from Quebranta grapes at Bodega San Isidro in Ica. Earthy and full, with banana, hay and pecan notes, and a standard choice for Pisco Sours.

name: Macchu Pisco
description: Peruvian pisco made only from Quebranta grapes and rested before bottling. Clean and dry, with grape, citrus and a light earthy finish. Widely used in US cocktail bars.

name: La Diablada Pisco
description: Acholado pisco from the makers of Macchu Pisco, blending aromatic and non-aromatic grape varieties. More floral and perfumed, with citrus blossom and soft fruit.

name: Capurro Acholado Pisco
description: Blended pisco from the Capurro family estate in Nazca, distilled once to proof from several grape varieties. Balanced between floral aromatics and a rounded, grapey body.

name: Caravedo Quebranta Pisco
description: Single grape pisco from Hacienda La Caravedo in Ica, a distillery dating to 1684. Dry and clean, with grape, green banana and a light nutty finish.

name: Caravedo Mosto Verde Pisco
description: Mosto verde pisco from Hacienda La Caravedo, formerly sold as Pisco Portón. Distilled from partially fermented must for a fuller, silkier texture with floral and citrus notes.
image_query: Caravedo Mosto Verde Pisco Porton bottle

name: Pisco 1615 Quebranta
description: Peruvian puro pisco distilled from Quebranta grapes in the Ica Valley, named for the year of the earliest pisco record. Dry, with grape, pear and a soft earthy note.

name: Demonio de los Andes Quebranta Pisco
description: Quebranta pisco from Tacama, a long established wine estate in Ica. Clean and rounded, with grape, banana and a light almond note.
image_query: Demonio de los Andes Quebranta Pisco bottle

name: El Gobernador Pisco
description: Chilean pisco made by Miguel Torres Chile from Muscat grapes grown in the Limarí Valley. Very aromatic, with rose, jasmine and citrus peel.

name: Waqar Pisco
description: Chilean pisco distilled from Muscat grapes grown in the foothills of the Andes at Tulahuén. Clear and perfumed, with floral, pear and citrus notes.

name: Singani 63
description: Bolivian singani brought to export markets by film director Steven Soderbergh. Distilled from high altitude Muscat of Alexandria grapes, floral and crisp, with a clean finish.

name: Nardini Grappa Bianca
description: Unaged grappa from Nardini of Bassano del Grappa, distilling since 1779. Bottled at 50 percent, dry and punchy, with grape skin, herbs and a clean finish.

name: Nonino Grappa Il Moscato
description: Single variety grappa from the Nonino family in Friuli, distilled from fresh Moscato pomace. Fragrant and soft, with rose, sage and ripe grape.
image_query: Nonino Grappa Monovitigno Il Moscato bottle

name: Poli Sarpa di Poli Grappa
description: Young grappa from the Poli distillery in Schiavon, distilled from Merlot and Cabernet pomace in copper pot stills. Dry and herbaceous, with fresh grape and mint.
image_query: Poli Sarpa di Poli Grappa bottle

name: Torres 10 Brandy
description: Spanish brandy from the Torres family in Penedès, aged in American oak by the solera system. Warm and rounded, with vanilla, cinnamon and dried fruit. A common value pour.

name: Lustau Solera Reserva Brandy de Jerez
description: Brandy de Jerez from sherry house Lustau, aged by the solera system in casks seasoned with sherry. Dry and nutty, with walnut, toffee and dried fruit.
image_query: Lustau Brandy de Jerez Solera Reserva bottle

name: Cardenal Mendoza Solera Gran Reserva Brandy
description: Brandy de Jerez from Sánchez Romate, aged for many years in oloroso and Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Dark and rich, with raisin, prune, chocolate and walnut.
image_query: Cardenal Mendoza Solera Gran Reserva Brandy bottle

name: Carlos I Solera Gran Reserva Brandy
description: Brandy de Jerez from Osborne, aged by the solera system in sherry casks. Smooth and sweet-edged, with vanilla, cocoa, toasted nuts and caramel.
image_query: Carlos I Solera Gran Reserva Brandy de Jerez bottle

name: Metaxa 12 Stars
description: Greek amber spirit that blends aged wine distillates with Muscat wine from Samos and a botanical infusion. Rich and smooth, with dried fig, orange peel, chocolate and toffee.

name: Metaxa 7 Stars
description: The mid-range Metaxa, blending aged wine distillates with Samos Muscat wine and botanicals. Mellow and lightly sweet, with peach, apricot, honey and vanilla.

name: Vecchia Romagna Etichetta Nera
match: Vecchia Romagna Etichetta Nera Italian Brandy
description: Italy's best known brandy, distilled from Trebbiano wine and aged in oak, sold in a triangular bottle. Soft and mellow, with vanilla, dried fruit and toasted wood.
image_query: Vecchia Romagna Etichetta Nera brandy bottle

name: Asbach Uralt
description: German brandy made in Rüdesheim am Rhein since 1892 and aged in Limousin oak. Mild and rounded, with plum, vanilla and nut. Used in Rüdesheimer coffee.

name: E&J VSOP Brandy
description: California grape brandy from E&J Gallo and one of the top selling brandies in the USA. Sweet and smooth, with vanilla, maple and brown spice.

name: Korbel California Brandy
description: California brandy made since 1889 and the standard call for a Wisconsin Brandy Old Fashioned. Light and sweet, with vanilla, caramel and soft oak.

name: Argonaut Saloon Strength Brandy
description: California brandy blended from young and older pot and column still stocks and bottled at 91 proof for cocktails. Bright fruit, vanilla and oak, with enough weight to mix.

name: Bertoux Brandy
description: California pot still brandy blended with input from bartenders for use in classic cocktails. Fruity and bright, with apricot, orange blossom, honey and light oak.

name: Copper & Kings American Craft Brandy
description: Pot distilled grape brandy from Copper & Kings in Louisville, aged in bourbon barrels and new American oak. Bottled at 45 percent, with caramel, dried fruit and whiskey-like oak.
image_query: Copper & Kings American Craft Brandy bottle

name: St Agnes VS Brandy
description: Australian grape brandy from the Angove family's St Agnes Distillery in Renmark, pot distilled and aged at least two years in oak. Apricot, orange peel and vanilla.

name: Massenez Poire Williams
description: Williams pear eau-de-vie from G.E. Massenez, an Alsace distiller founded in 1870. Clear and dry, with a strong aroma of ripe pear.
image_query: Massenez Poire Williams eau de vie bottle

name: Massenez Kirsch Vieux
description: Cherry eau-de-vie from Massenez in Alsace, distilled from fermented cherries and rested before bottling. Dry, with cherry, marzipan and a clean finish.

name: Schladerer Kirschwasser
description: Black Forest cherry eau-de-vie from Schladerer in Staufen, a family distillery founded in 1844. Dry and aromatic, with cherry and bitter almond.

name: St. George Pear Brandy
description: Unaged pear eau-de-vie from St. George Spirits in Alameda, distilled from Bartlett pears. Clear and dry, with ripe pear, a hint of cinnamon and a buttery texture.

name: Clear Creek Pear Brandy
description: Williams pear eau-de-vie from Clear Creek Distillery, made from Oregon Bartlett pears. Clear and dry, with fresh pear skin and a soft floral note.

name: Purkhart Pear Williams Eau-de-Vie
description: Austrian Williams pear eau-de-vie imported to the USA by Haus Alpenz and common in cocktail bars. Dry and clean, with ripe pear and a light spice note.

name: Capreolus Raspberry Eau de Vie
description: English raspberry eau-de-vie from Capreolus Distillery in the Cotswolds, made in small vintage batches from local fruit. Intensely perfumed, dry and long.
image_query: Capreolus Raspberry Eau de Vie bottle

name: Bertrand Gentiane Eau-de-Vie
description: Gentian root spirit from Distillerie Bertrand in Uberach, Alsace, founded in 1874. Dry and clear, with an earthy, bitter, rooty aroma. Used in small measures.
image_query: Bertrand Eau de Vie de Gentiane bottle

name: Greensand Ridge Apricot Eau de Vie
description: English apricot eau-de-vie from Greensand Ridge Distillery in Kent, made from locally grown surplus fruit. Clean and dry, with a rich, ripe apricot flavour.
image_query: Greensand Ridge Apricot Eau de Vie bottle

name: Absinthe
description: High strength spirit flavoured with grand wormwood, green anise and fennel, originally from Switzerland and France. Turns cloudy with water and is often used as a rinse or in dashes.

name: Absinthe Blanche
description: Clear absinthe bottled straight after distillation without the final herb colouring step, a style tied to Switzerland's Val-de-Travers. Softer and often lower in strength than verte.

name: Pastis
description: French anise and liquorice aperitif, typically 40 to 45 percent, that became popular after absinthe was banned. Served long with cold water, which turns it cloudy, and used in rinses.

name: Ouzo
description: Greek anise flavoured spirit, distilled with aniseed and other botanicals such as fennel and mastic. Drunk with water or ice, which turns it milky white.

name: Sambuca
description: Italian anise liqueur flavoured with star anise and often elderflower, sweet and viscous. Served neat with coffee beans, alongside espresso, or as a shot.

name: Anisette
description: Sweet, lower strength anise liqueur made in France, Spain and Italy. Lighter than pastis or sambuca, and used in small amounts in classic cocktails.

name: Levantine Arak
description: Grape spirit redistilled with aniseed, traditional in Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Palestine and Israel. Unsweetened and strong, it is mixed with water and ice and turns milky white.

name: Raki
description: Turkish spirit distilled from grapes or raisins and redistilled with aniseed. Drunk diluted with cold water alongside meze, turning cloudy in the glass.

name: Pernod Absinthe
description: Absinthe from the brand that first commercialised the spirit in 1805, relaunched to a traditional recipe. Green, 68 percent, with strong anise, wormwood and herbal notes.

name: La Fée Parisienne Absinthe
description: French absinthe supérieure launched in 2000 with the Musée de l'Absinthe, the first traditional absinthe distilled in France since the 1915 ban. Green and strongly anise led.
image_query: La Fee Parisienne Absinthe Superieure bottle

name: St. George Absinthe Verte
description: California absinthe on a brandy base, the first legal American absinthe released after the US ban ended in 2007. Herbal and complex, with star anise, basil, tarragon and mint.

name: Kübler Absinthe
description: Clear Swiss absinthe from the Val-de-Travers, the birthplace of the spirit, made to a family recipe from 1863. Soft and sweet-seeming, with anise, fennel and alpine herbs.

name: La Clandestine Absinthe
description: Clear Swiss absinthe from Couvet in the Val-de-Travers, based on a bootleg recipe from the ban years. Delicate and floral, with anise, mint and alpine herbs.

name: Vieux Pontarlier Absinthe
description: French absinthe from the Émile Pernot distillery in Pontarlier, distilled in old alembics with local wormwood. Green, 65 percent, with anise, fennel and a dry herbal finish.

name: Lucid Absinthe Supérieure
description: French distilled absinthe created by T.A. Breaux and the first genuine absinthe approved for sale in the USA in 2007. Pale green, with anise, fennel and a gentle bitterness.

name: Jade Nouvelle-Orléans Absinthe
description: Absinthe made by T.A. Breaux at the Combier distillery in Saumur as a tribute to New Orleans. Floral and herbal, with anise and a long, layered finish. Favoured for Sazeracs.

name: Hendrick's Absinthe
description: Absinthe from the makers of Hendrick's Gin, bottled at a lower 48 percent for mixing. Wormwood and star anise sit alongside the brand's rose and cucumber notes.

name: Ricard Pastis
description: The original pastis de Marseille, created by Paul Ricard in 1932. Flavoured with star anise, liquorice and Provençal herbs, and served one part to five parts cold water.

name: Pernod Anise
description: French anise spirit made from distilled star anise and fennel with herbs, lighter and less liquorice heavy than pastis. A common absinthe stand-in for rinses and in cooking.

name: Pastis 51
description: Pastis de Marseille launched in 1951 and one of the two big pastis brands in France. Anise and liquorice, slightly softer than Ricard, served with cold water.

name: Henri Bardouin Pastis
description: Craft pastis from Distilleries et Domaines de Provence in Forcalquier, made with more than 65 herbs and spices. More complex and spicier than the mainstream brands.

name: Herbsaint
description: New Orleans anise liqueur first sold in 1934 as an absinthe substitute, now made by Sazerac. The traditional rinse for a Sazerac, with anise and a light herbal sweetness.

name: Ouzo 12
description: One of the most widely exported ouzo brands, first made in 1880 and named after barrel number 12. Clean anise with a little sweetness, served with ice and water.

name: Ouzo Plomari
description: Ouzo from the Isidoros Arvanitis distillery in Plomari on Lesbos, the island most closely tied to the spirit. Smooth, with aniseed, fennel and a faint herbal sweetness.
image_query: Ouzo of Plomari Isidoros Arvanitis bottle

name: Luxardo Sambuca dei Cesari
description: Clear sambuca from Luxardo, made with star anise and green anise distillates. Sweet and full, with a clean anise flavour. Served neat, with coffee beans or in coffee.

name: Molinari Sambuca Extra
description: Italy's leading sambuca, made in Civitavecchia since 1945 from star anise. Sweet, rich and strongly anise flavoured, traditionally served with three coffee beans.

name: Antica Sambuca Classic
description: Clear Italian sambuca that is a staple shot pour in UK and Australian bars. Sweet and smooth, with star anise and a touch of elderflower.

name: Ramazzotti Sambuca
description: Clear sambuca from the Milanese amaro house Ramazzotti. Sweet and rounded, with star anise and a soft, warming finish.

name: Marie Brizard Anisette
description: French anisette made in Bordeaux to a recipe dating from 1755, flavoured with green anise and other botanicals. Sweet, light and delicately anise scented.

name: Anís del Mono Dulce
description: Sweet Spanish anise liqueur made in Badalona since 1870, sold in a distinctive diamond cut bottle. Clear, sugary and strongly flavoured with aniseed.

name: Massaya Arak
description: Lebanese arak from the Massaya estate in the Bekaa Valley, distilled from Obeidi grapes with aniseed and rested in clay jars. Dry, strong and clean, served with water and ice.

name: Yeni Rakı
description: The best selling Turkish rakı, distilled from grapes and raisins and flavoured with aniseed. Dry and firm, drunk with cold water and ice alongside food.

name: Sake
description: Japanese brewed rice drink made from polished rice, water, koji and yeast, usually 14 to 16 percent. Ranges from dry and crisp to fruity and rich, and is served chilled or warm.

name: Junmai Sake
description: Sake made only from rice, water, koji and yeast, with no added distilled alcohol. Tends to be fuller and more savoury, with a rice forward flavour and good acidity.

name: Junmai Ginjo Sake
description: Pure rice sake brewed from rice polished to 60 percent or less of its size and fermented cool. Aromatic and fruity, with a light, clean body.

name: Junmai Daiginjo Sake
description: Pure rice sake brewed from rice polished to 50 percent or less of its original size. A refined grade that is delicate, fragrant and smooth, best served chilled.

name: Nigori Sake
description: Coarsely filtered sake that keeps some rice sediment, giving a cloudy white look. Creamy, soft and usually on the sweeter side. Shake gently before pouring.

name: Sparkling Sake
description: Carbonated sake, often low in alcohol and lightly sweet. The bubbles come from a second fermentation in the bottle or from added carbonation.

name: Shochu
description: Japanese distilled spirit made with koji from barley, sweet potato, rice or other bases, mostly in Kyushu. Usually bottled around 25 percent and drunk with water, soda or ice.

name: Barley Shochu
description: Shochu distilled from barley (mugi), centred on Oita and the island of Iki in Nagasaki. Light, clean and gently nutty, and the easiest style to mix.

name: Sweet Potato Shochu
description: Shochu distilled from sweet potatoes (imo), the signature style of Kagoshima and Miyazaki. Earthy and aromatic, with a rich, sweet, roasted character.

name: Rice Shochu
description: Shochu distilled from rice (kome) and rice koji, with the Kuma region of Kumamoto as its home. Clean and delicate, with a soft fragrance that recalls sake.

name: Awamori
description: Okinawan spirit distilled from long grain Thai rice fermented with black koji. Earthy and full flavoured, commonly 25 to 30 percent, with aged versions called kusu.

name: Soju
description: Korean clear spirit. Common green bottle soju is diluted neutral spirit with sweeteners at 16 to 20 percent, while traditional soju is distilled from rice and is stronger.

name: Baijiu
description: Chinese grain spirit, usually sorghum based, fermented with qu in pits or jars and distilled in the solid state. Pungent and strong, and grouped by aroma: strong, light, sauce and rice.

name: Umeshu
description: Japanese liqueur made by steeping unripe ume fruit and sugar in shochu, neutral spirit or sake. Sweet and tart, with an almond note from the stones.

name: Yuzushu
description: Japanese liqueur made by blending yuzu juice with sake or shochu and sugar. Low in alcohol, tart and fragrant, and often served chilled or with soda.

name: Makgeolli
description: Korean unfiltered rice brew fermented with nuruk, milky white and lightly sparkling. Around 6 percent, with a sweet, tangy taste. Shake or stir before pouring.

name: Arrack
description: South and Southeast Asian spirit. Batavia arrack from Java is distilled from sugarcane molasses with red rice, and Ceylon arrack from coconut flower sap. A classic punch base.

name: Dassai 45 Junmai Daiginjo
description: Junmai daiginjo from Asahi Shuzo in Yamaguchi, brewed from Yamada Nishiki rice polished to 45 percent. Fruity and clean, with melon, pear and a soft, slightly sweet finish.

name: Dassai 23 Junmai Daiginjo
description: Dassai's top regular bottling, brewed from Yamada Nishiki rice polished down to 23 percent of the grain. Very delicate and aromatic, with honeyed fruit and a long, clean finish.

name: Hakutsuru Excellent Junmai
description: Everyday junmai sake from Hakutsuru in Kobe's Nada district, one of Japan's largest brewers. Dry and mellow with a full rice flavour, good chilled, warm or in cocktails.

name: Hakutsuru Sayuri Nigori
description: Cloudy, coarse filtered junmai sake from Hakutsuru in a pink frosted bottle. Creamy and lightly sweet, with a soft floral aroma. Widely sold outside Japan.

name: Gekkeikan Traditional Sake
description: Junmai sake brewed in Folsom, California by Gekkeikan, a Kyoto brewer founded in 1637. Dry and mellow, with herbal and grapefruit hints. A standard house sake in the USA.

name: Ozeki Sake Dry
description: Dry junmai sake brewed in Hollister, California by Ozeki, a Hyogo brewer founded in 1711. Light and crisp with a clean finish, commonly used as a house pour and for cooking.

name: Sho Chiku Bai Classic Junmai
description: Junmai sake brewed in Berkeley, California by Takara Sake USA and a top seller in America. Full bodied and dry, good warm or chilled, and a common bar and kitchen sake.
image_query: Sho Chiku Bai Classic Junmai sake bottle

name: Tozai Living Jewel Junmai
description: Junmai sake brewed in Kyoto for the export label Tozai. Light and easy, with white grape, anise and a touch of sweet rice. Priced for by the glass pours and cocktails.
image_query: Tozai Living Jewel Junmai sake bottle

name: Tozai Snow Maiden Junmai Nigori
description: Cloudy junmai nigori from the export label Tozai, brewed in Kyoto. Creamy but fairly dry for the style, with honeydew melon, pumpkin and fresh rice.
image_query: Tozai Snow Maiden Junmai Nigori sake bottle

name: Mio Sparkling Sake
description: Low alcohol sparkling sake from Takara Shuzo, sold in a small blue bottle. Sweet, gently fizzy and fruity, with grape and pear notes.
image_query: Sho Chiku Bai Mio Sparkling Sake bottle

name: Hakkaisan Tokubetsu Honjozo
description: Special honjozo from Hakkaisan Brewery in Niigata, made with soft snowmelt water. Crisp, dry and clean in the Niigata style, and good warm or cold.

name: Kubota Senju
description: Ginjo sake from Asahi Shuzo in Niigata and the core bottling of the Kubota range. Dry, light and restrained, made to go with food.

name: Akashi-Tai Honjozo Tokubetsu
description: Special honjozo from Akashi Sake Brewery in Hyogo, a small brewer widely distributed in the UK. Medium bodied and dry, with citrus and straw notes, served warm or cold.

name: iichiko Silhouette Shochu
description: Barley shochu from Sanwa Shurui in Oita and the flagship of Japan's best known barley shochu brand. Light and clean, with white peach and a soft grain note.

name: iichiko Saiten Shochu
description: Barley shochu from iichiko bottled at 43 percent and developed with bartenders for cocktails. Fuller and more savoury, with melon, white grape, soy and citrus notes.

name: The SG Shochu Kome
description: Rice shochu from bartender Shingo Gokan's SG Group, made by Takahashi Shuzo in Kumamoto and bottled at 40 percent for mixing. Fragrant and fruity, like a ginjo sake in spirit form.

name: The SG Shochu Mugi
description: Barley shochu from the SG Group, made by Sanwa Shurui in Oita and bottled at 40 percent for cocktails. Toasty and rounded, with roasted grain and a little oak.

name: The SG Shochu Imo
description: Sweet potato shochu from the SG Group, made by Satsuma Shuzo in Kagoshima and bottled at 38 percent. Floral and earthy, with lychee and roasted sweet potato.

name: Kuro Kirishima Shochu
description: Sweet potato shochu from Kirishima Shuzo in Miyazaki, made with black koji, and one of Japan's top selling shochu. Rich and sweet, with a crisp finish.

name: Hakutake Shiro Shochu
description: Rice shochu from Takahashi Shuzo in the Kuma region of Kumamoto, vacuum distilled for a light style. Clean and delicate, with a gentle sake-like aroma.

name: Mizu Saga Barley Shochu
description: Single distilled barley shochu from Munemasa Shuzo in Saga, bottled at 35 percent for the US market. Round and grainy, with melon and a young whisky-like character.

name: Zanpa White Awamori
description: Light style awamori from Higa Shuzo in Yomitan, Okinawa, and one of the island's most popular everyday bottles. Fruity and clean, drunk with water, ice or soda.

name: Jinro Chamisul Fresh Soju
description: The world's best selling soju, from HiteJinro, filtered through bamboo charcoal. Clean, neutral and lightly sweet, sold in the familiar green bottle.

name: Jinro Chamisul Original Soju
description: The stronger, red cap version of Jinro's Chamisul soju. Clean and neutral with more bite than Fresh, often preferred for mixing with beer.
image_query: Jinro Chamisul Original soju red cap bottle

name: Jinro Grapefruit Soju
description: Grapefruit flavoured soju from HiteJinro at a lower 13 percent. Sweet and citrusy, drunk chilled as a shot or lengthened with soda.

name: Chum Churum Soju
description: Soju from Lotte Chilsung made with alkaline water, and the main rival to Jinro in Korea. Soft, clean and slightly sweet.

name: Hwayo 25 Soju
description: Premium Korean soju distilled from 100 percent rice and rested in onggi clay pots. Clean and soft, with a delicate rice aroma. Drunk neat, on ice or in cocktails.

name: Hwayo 41 Soju
description: Full strength rice soju from Hwayo, distilled from Korean rice and aged in clay pots. Rich and smooth, with a clear rice character, and used like a white spirit in cocktails.

name: Hwayo 19 Gold Soju
description: Lower strength rice soju from Hwayo that blends clay pot aged spirit with oak aged spirit. Soft and rounded, with rice sweetness and a light oak note.

name: Tokki Soju White Label
description: Craft rice soju started in Brooklyn and now made in Chungju, Korea, from glutinous rice, nuruk and water. Clean and lightly sweet, with a soft rice finish.

name: Tokki Soju Black Label
description: The 40 percent version of Tokki's traditional rice soju, distilled from glutinous rice and nuruk. Fuller and more aromatic, and used like a white spirit in cocktails.

name: Kweichow Moutai
description: China's most famous baijiu, a sauce aroma spirit made from sorghum and wheat in Maotai town, Guizhou. Savoury and complex, with soy, fermented bean and tropical fruit notes.
image_query: Kweichow Moutai Flying Fairy baijiu bottle

name: Ming River Sichuan Baijiu
description: Strong aroma baijiu made by Luzhou Laojiao in Sichuan and aimed at bartenders outside China. Pineapple, anise and a funky, cheese-like note that works in tropical style drinks.

name: Wuliangye
description: Strong aroma baijiu from Yibin, Sichuan, distilled from five grains: sorghum, rice, glutinous rice, wheat and corn. Fruity and fragrant, with pineapple and a long finish.

name: Luzhou Laojiao Guojiao 1573
description: Premium strong aroma baijiu from Luzhou Laojiao in Sichuan, named for fermentation pits in use since 1573. Sweet and fruity, with a mellow, lingering finish.

name: Red Star Erguotou
description: Inexpensive light aroma baijiu from Beijing, sold in small green bottles and drunk across northern China. Sharp and clean, with sorghum sweetness and a hot finish.

name: Kinmen Kaoliang 58
description: Taiwanese sorghum spirit from the island of Kinmen, a light aroma style of baijiu. Very strong at 58 percent, clean and fragrant, with a sweet grain finish.

name: Tabb Baijiu Raw
description: Modern baijiu from the brand Tabb, made with cocktail bars in mind. Light and smooth, with pineapple, apple and pear notes, a little minerality and a clean finish.

name: The Choya Single Year Umeshu
description: Umeshu from Choya, Japan's largest producer, made only from Kishu Nanko ume, sugar and spirit and aged around a year. Sweet and tart, with fresh ume and marzipan notes.
image_query: The Choya Single Year umeshu bottle

name: Choya Extra Years Umeshu
description: Longer aged umeshu from Choya, with the ume fruit steeped for up to three years. Richer and deeper than the Single Year, with dried fruit and almond.

name: Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
description: Umeshu from Akashi Sake Brewery in Hyogo, made by steeping ume in ginjo sake. Rich and sweet, with plum, almond and a sherry-like depth.

name: Mii no Kotobuki Umeshu
description: Umeshu from the Mii no Kotobuki brewery in Fukuoka, made by steeping ume in aged junmai sake. Tart and savoury for the style, with less sugar than most umeshu.
image_query: Mii no Kotobuki Mii no Umeshu bottle

name: Umenoyado Aragoshi Umeshu
description: Cloudy umeshu from Umenoyado Brewery in Nara, with pureed ume flesh blended back into the liqueur. Thick, juicy and tart, served over ice or with soda.

name: Akashi-Tai Ginjo Yuzushu
description: Yuzu liqueur from Akashi Sake Brewery in Hyogo, made by blending yuzu juice with ginjo sake. Bright, sharp and fragrant, with a sweet and sour balance.

name: Umenoyado Yuzushu
description: Yuzu liqueur from Umenoyado Brewery in Nara, blending plenty of yuzu juice with sake. Cloudy, tart and refreshing, like a grown-up lemonade.

name: Kooksoondang Makgeolli
description: Widely exported makgeolli from Kooksoondang, one of Korea's largest traditional brewers. Milky, lightly fizzy and gently sweet, with a tangy rice flavour.

name: Batavia Arrack van Oosten
description: Indonesian arrack distilled on Java from sugarcane molasses with fermented red rice, bottled at 50 percent. Funky and smoky, and used in small measures in punches and tiki drinks.
